conteudo_completo:
O São Paulo Futebol Clube possui 41 títulos oficiais principais. Título oficial é a conquista de uma competição promovida e institucionalizada no calendário das federações às quais o Tricolor está filiado (FPF, CBF, Conmebol, FIFA). Contudo, algumas dessas competições, por terem sido poucas vezes realizadas ou por terem sido criadas somente para preencher brechas temporárias de calendário são, por assim dizer, não tão importantes. Por isso a distinção “títulos oficiais principais”. Neste trabalho, tais competições são apresentadas com texto em negrito. As oficiais menores surgem logo em sequência, sem qualquer grifo.

Existem ainda outras competições, organizadas por clubes ou federações às quais o São Paulo não se encontra filiado. São, assim, competições amistosas, não oficiais no aspecto federativo (mas seus jogos são oficiais para os clube – visto que são autorizados e normatizados pelas federações, mesmo assim). Resumindo: jogos amistosos são jogos oficiais, mas competições amistosas não são competições oficiais.

Por fim, há também o caso das taças secundárias. Troféus adquiridos como uma espécie de bônus em alguma competição cuja principal premiação era outra taça. Geralmente ocorrem em casos ofertados por patrocinadores ou em homenagens de terceiros.

O São Paulo Futebol Clube possui 42 títulos oficiais principais. Título oficial é a conquista de uma competição promovida e institucionalizada no calendário das federações às quais o Tricolor está filiado (FPF, CBF, Conmebol, FIFA). Contudo, algumas dessas competições, por terem sido poucas vezes realizadas ou por terem sido criadas somente para preencher brechas temporárias de calendário são, por assim dizer, não tão importantes. Por isso a distinção “títulos oficiais principais”. Neste trabalho, tais competições são apresentadas com texto em negrito. As oficiais menores surgem logo em sequência, sem qualquer grifo.

Existem ainda outras competições, organizadas por clubes ou federações às quais o São Paulo não se encontra filiado. São, assim, competições amistosas, não oficiais no aspecto federativo (mas seus jogos são oficiais para os clube – visto que são autorizados e normatizados pelas federações, mesmo assim). Resumindo: jogos amistosos são jogos oficiais, mas competições amistosas não são competições oficiais.

Por fim, há também o caso das taças secundárias. Troféus adquiridos como uma espécie de bônus em alguma competição cuja principal premiação era outra taça. Geralmente ocorrem em casos ofertados por patrocinadores ou em homenagens de terceiros.

São Paulo is one of the most successful teams in Brazil with 44 official titles, that includes 23 state titles, 1 inter-state title, 6 Campeonato Brasileiro titles, 1 Copa do Brasil title, 1 Supercopa do Brasil title, 3 Copa Libertadores titles, 1 Copa Sudamericana, 1 Supercopa Libertadores, 1 Copa CONMEBOL, 1 Copa Masters CONMEBOL, 2 Recopa Sudamericanas, 2 Intercontinental Cup "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") and 1 FIFA Club World Cup. It is the only club in the country to have won all available titles, earning the nickname "Champions of All", an honour achieved after winning the 2024 Supercopa do Brasil.

All five FIFA World Cups won by Brazil contained at least one São Paulo player, an honour shared with cross-city rivals Palmeiras.

**São Paulo Futebol Clube** (Brazilian Portuguese: [[sɐ̃w ˈpawlu futʃiˈbɔw ˈklubi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:Sao-paulo-futebol-clube-pronunciation-ptbr.ogg "File:Sao-paulo-futebol-clube-pronunciation-ptbr.ogg")) is a Brazilian professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the [Morumbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morumbi,_São_Paulo "Morumbi, São Paulo") district of [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo"). It plays in [Campeonato Paulista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Paulista "Campeonato Paulista"), the [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state) "São Paulo (state)")'s premier [state league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_football_leagues_in_Brazil "State football leagues in Brazil"), and in the [Campeonato Brasileiro Série A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), the top tier of [Brazilian football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_football "Brazilian football"). Despite being primarily a football club, São Paulo competes in a [wide variety of sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_São_Paulo_FC_records_and_statistics "List of São Paulo FC records and statistics"). Its home ground is the multipurpose 67,052-seater [Estádio do Morumbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_do_Morumbi "Estádio do Morumbi"), the biggest private-owned field in Brazil. São Paulo is part of the [Big Twelve of Brazilian football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Twelve_(Brazilian_football) "Big Twelve (Brazilian football)"), South America's biggest worldwide champion — with three world titles, along [Boca Juniors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boca_Juniors "Boca Juniors"), [Peñarol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peñarol "Peñarol"), and [Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Nacional_de_Futbol "Club Nacional de Futbol") — and one of the only two clubs that have [never been relegated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unrelegated_association_football_clubs "List of unrelegated association football clubs") from Brazil's top division, the other being [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CR_Flamengo "CR Flamengo").[[3]](#cite_note-PlacarFeb24-3)

Founded in 1930 from a merger between the [Club Athletico Paulistano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Athletico_Paulistano "Club Athletico Paulistano") and the [Associação Atlética das Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Atlética_das_Palmeiras "Associação Atlética das Palmeiras"), the club has used its traditional home kit of a white shirt with two horizontal stripes (one red and one black), white shorts, and white socks[[4]](#cite_note-autogenerated1-4) since its inception; the color choice was made in honour of its parent-clubs primary colors, and also to represent the colors of the state of [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state) "São Paulo (state)"). Although its main affiliation is with the state and city where it was founded, São Paulo is a national team and the third best-supported club in Brazil, with over 22 million supporters, covering around 9.9% of its population. Their supporters are called *são-paulinos* and are often nicknamed *Torcida que conduz* (Supporters who lead), due to their importance in maintaining São Paulo's long lasting relevance in South America's football. São Paulo ranked fifth in Brazil with a market value of R$ 2.214 billion in 2023.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

São Paulo is one of the most successful teams in Brazil with 44 official titles, that includes 23 state titles, 1 inter-state title, 6 [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") titles, 1 [Copa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_do_Brasil "Copa do Brasil") title, 1 [Supercopa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_do_Brasil "Supercopa do Brasil") title, 3 [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") titles, 1 [Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sudamericana "Copa Sudamericana"), 1 [Supercopa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_Libertadores "Supercopa Libertadores"), 1 [Copa CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_CONMEBOL "Copa CONMEBOL"), 1 [Copa Masters CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Masters_CONMEBOL "Copa Masters CONMEBOL"), 2 [Recopa Sudamericanas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recopa_Sudamericana "Recopa Sudamericana"), 2 [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960–2004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") and 1 [FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup "FIFA Club World Cup").[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)[[9]](#cite_note-9) It is the only club in the country to have won all available titles, earning the nickname "Champions of All", an honour achieved after winning the [2024 Supercopa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Supercopa_do_Brasil "2024 Supercopa do Brasil").

All five [FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") won by [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") contained at least one São Paulo player, an honour shared with cross-city rivals [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SE_Palmeiras "SE Palmeiras").[[10]](#cite_note-10)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of São Paulo FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_São_Paulo_FC "History of São Paulo FC")

### 1930–1934: Origins: "São Paulo da Floresta" ("São Paulo of the Forest")

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1930–1934: Origins: ")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Memorial_-_foundation_-_01.jpg/250px-Memorial_-_foundation_-_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Memorial_-_foundation_-_01.jpg)

The foundations of the team in 1930 and 1935 at the memorial Cássio Luiz dos Santos Werneck.

 [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/SPFC_squad_-_1931_-_02.jpg/250px-SPFC_squad_-_1931_-_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SPFC_squad_-_1931_-_02.jpg)

The championship team of 1931

São Paulo Futebol Clube was founded on 25 January 1930 by 60 former officials, players, members, and friends of the football clubs [Club Athletico Paulistano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Athletico_Paulistano "Club Athletico Paulistano") and [Associação Atlética das Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Atlética_das_Palmeiras "Associação Atlética das Palmeiras") of São Paulo. Club Athletico Paulistano, founded in 1900 and one of the oldest clubs in town and 11-time champions of São Paulo, abandoned football due to the professionalization of the sport. Associação Atlética das Palmeiras, founded in 1902 and three-time champions of São Paulo, intended after the end of the season 1929 to set up a professional team, but failed to do so.[[11]](#cite_note-História-11)

The jerseys of the new club were derived from Associação Atlética das Palmeiras, which were white and sported a black ring across the chest. To the black-and-white of Associação Atlética das Palmeiras was added the red-and-white of Club Athletico Paulistano, and the ring became red, white, and black.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

The Club Athletico Paulistano brought to the union star players [Arthur Friedenreich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Friedenreich "Arthur Friedenreich")[[13]](#cite_note-13) and [Araken Patusca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Araken_Patusca "Araken Patusca").[[14]](#cite_note-14) Associação Atlética das Palmeiras' contribution was the stadium [Estádio da Floresta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chácara_da_Floresta "Chácara da Floresta"), generally known as *Chácara da Floresta*.[[15]](#cite_note-Fundação-15) In August 1930, São Paulo played a match against the [United States national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_soccer_team "United States men's national soccer team"), which had competed in the [Uruguay World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1930_FIFA_World_Cup "1930 FIFA World Cup"), at Chácara da Floresta wearing the uniform of AA das Palmeiras; São Paulo won its first international match 5-3.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

Internal arguments and turmoil led to financial problems. The club merged with Clube de Regatas Tietê, another sports club from the town, and the football department was disbanded on 14 May 1935.[[15]](#cite_note-Fundação-15)

### 1935–1939: The rebirth of São Paulo FC

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1935–1939: The rebirth of São Paulo FC")]

Just after the merger with Tietê, the founders and re-founders created the Grêmio Tricolor, which formed Clube Atlético São Paulo on 4 June 1935, and, finally, São Paulo Futebol Clube on 16 December of the same year.[[17]](#cite_note-origins-17)

The new club's first game was against [Portuguesa Santista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Atlética_Portuguesa_Santista "Associação Atlética Portuguesa Santista") on 25 January 1936. The match was almost cancelled, owing to the city's anniversary, but Porphyrio da Paz, the football director and composer of the club's anthem, obtained permission from the Board of Education Office for the game to continue.[[18]](#cite_note-30s-18)

Another merger occurred in 1938, this time with Clube Atlético Estudantes Paulista, from the neighborhood of [Moóca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moóca "Moóca"), and the club finished as runners-up in the Campeonato Paulista.

### 1940–1950: "The Steam Roller"

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1940–1950: ")]

In 1940, when the [Estádio do Pacaembu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_do_Pacaembu "Estádio do Pacaembu") was inaugurated, a new era began in [São Paulo state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_(state) "São Paulo (state)") football. São Paulo Futebol Clube finished as runners-up once again in the Campeonato Paulista in 1941, and a year later the club paid 200 [contos de réis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real") (equivalent to approximately R$162,000 today) to acquire [Leônidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leônidas_(footballer,_born_1913) "Leônidas (footballer, born 1913)") from [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo "Clube de Regatas do Flamengo"). During this period, São Paulo also acquired the [Argentinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentinian_people "Argentinian people") [António Sastre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Sastre "Antonio Sastre") and [Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_people "Brazilian people") [Noronha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noronha_(footballer,_born_1918) "Noronha (footballer, born 1918)"), [José Carlos Bauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Carlos_Bauer "José Carlos Bauer"), [Zezé Procópio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zezé_Procópio "Zezé Procópio"), [Luizinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luisinho_(footballer,_born_1911) "Luisinho (footballer, born 1911)"), [Rui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rui_Campos "Rui Campos") and Teixeirinha. With these new additions, *Tricolor* became known as the *Steam Roller*, winning the Paulista championship five times, in 1943, 1945, 1946, 1948 and 1949. The club sold its [Canindé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_do_Canindé "Estádio do Canindé") training ground to [Portuguesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Portuguesa_de_Desportos "Associação Portuguesa de Desportos") to raise money for their new stadium, the [Estádio do Morumbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_do_Morumbi "Estádio do Morumbi"), for which construction began in 1952.

### 1951–1957: The dry spell

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1951–1957: The dry spell")]

The run of success of the 1940s, came to an end in the early 1950s, and the club only won two state championships in the new decade, in 1953 and 1957. The 1957 championship was won with the help of the 35-year-old Brazilian international [Zizinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zizinho "Zizinho"), and Hungarian manager [Béla Guttmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Béla_Guttmann "Béla Guttmann"), both of them becoming idols. Guttmann took charge of the team in 1957 and won the [São Paulo State Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Paulista "Campeonato Paulista") that year.[[19]](#cite_note-auto2-19)[[20]](#cite_note-auto8-20) While in Brazil he helped popularise the [4–2–4 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_(association_football)#4–2–4 "Formation (association football)"), which was subsequently used by [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") as they won the [1958 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup "1958 FIFA World Cup").

In the years that followed, the club struggled to compete with the rise of [Pelé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelé "Pelé") and his club, Santos. With the construction of the Morumbi stadium still ongoing, São Paulo entered its longest period without a title in its history, which was to last 13 years.

### 1958–1969: Just the stadium

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1958–1969: Just the stadium")]

Since São Paulo's budget planning was focused on the Estádio do Morumbi construction rather than the signing of new players, few expensive players were bought during the 1960s, although the club did acquire Brazilian internationals [Roberto Dias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Dias "Roberto Dias") and [Jurandir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurandir_de_Freitas "Jurandir de Freitas"). In 1960, the Estádio do Morumbi was inaugurated, named after the late Cícero Pompeu de Toledo, the club's chairman during most of the stadium construction.[[21]](#cite_note-21) One of the few happy moments for the fans during this period was the 1963 Paulista Championship 4–1 victory against Pelé's Santos.

### 1970–1979: Campeonato Brasileiro (Brazilian Championship)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1970–1979: Campeonato Brasileiro (Brazilian Championship)")]

In 1970, the Estádio do Morumbi was finally completed and the club purchased [Gérson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gérson "Gérson") from [Botafogo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botafogo_de_Futebol_e_Regatas "Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas"), Uruguayan midfielder [Pedro Rocha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Rocha_(Uruguayan_footballer) "Pedro Rocha (Uruguayan footballer)") from [Peñarol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peñarol "Peñarol") and striker [Toninho Guerreiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toninho_Guerreiro "Toninho Guerreiro") from Santos. The club was managed by [Zezé Moreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zezé_Moreira "Zezé Moreira"), who was the manager of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") at the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") in [1954](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_FIFA_World_Cup "1954 FIFA World Cup"), and won the Paulista Championship after beating [Guarani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guarani_Futebol_Clube "Guarani Futebol Clube") 2–1 in the [Campinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campinas "Campinas") a week before the end of the competition.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Vista_a%C3%A9rea_do_Est%C3%A1dio_do_Morumbi%2C_23_jan_1970.tif/lossless-page1-250px-Vista_a%C3%A9rea_do_Est%C3%A1dio_do_Morumbi%2C_23_jan_1970.tif.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vista_aérea_do_Estádio_do_Morumbi,_23_jan_1970.tif)

View of the Morumbi Stadium, 23 January 1970. [National Archives of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_National_Archives "Brazilian National Archives").

In 1971, the club beat [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedade_Esportiva_Palmeiras "Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras") 1–0 with a goal from [Toninho Guerreiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toninho_Guerreiro "Toninho Guerreiro") in the final to capture another state title. That year saw the inaugural [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), with the club finishing as runners-up to [Atlético Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atlético_Mineiro "Clube Atlético Mineiro"), managed by [Telê Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telê_Santana "Telê Santana").

In the following years, São Paulo and Palmeiras gradually overtook Pelé's Santos and [Corinthians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Corinthians_Paulista "Sport Club Corinthians Paulista") as the dominant club sides in São Paulo state. In 1972, Palmeiras won the state championship title, only one point ahead of São Paulo, and the following year the clubs finished in the same positions in the [Brazilian Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "1973 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"). In 1974, São Paulo took part in the [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_Copa_Libertadores "1974 Copa Libertadores") losing in the final to [Independiente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Independiente "Club Atlético Independiente") in a replay.

In 1975, former goalkeeper [José Poy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Poy "José Poy") took over as manager, and São Paulo won the Paulista Championship after defeating [Portuguesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Portuguesa_de_Desportos "Associação Portuguesa de Desportos") in a penalty shoot-out.

[Valdir Peres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valdir_Peres "Valdir Peres"), [Chicão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicão_(footballer,_born_1949) "Chicão (footballer, born 1949)"), [Serginho Chulapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serginho_Chulapa "Serginho Chulapa") and [Zé Sérgio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zé_Sérgio "Zé Sérgio") were the club's most influential players when São Paulo finally secured the Brazilian Championship for the first time in [1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "1977 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") following a penalty shoot-out victory over Atlético Mineiro at the [Mineirão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineirão "Mineirão"). However, they failed to win another trophy until the reclaimed the Paulista Championship in 1980.

### The 1980s: Tricolor decade

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: The 1980s: Tricolor decade")]

In the 1980s, São Paulo won four Paulista and one Brazilian titles, helped by the impressive central defensive pair of [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_(footballer,_born_1954) "Oscar (footballer, born 1954)") and [Dario Pereyra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dario_Pereyra "Dario Pereyra"). 1980 and 1981, the club won the Paulista Championship in successive seasons for the first time since the 1940s.[[22]](#cite_note-80s-22)

In 1985, the head coach [Cilinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilinho "Cilinho") introduced to the world the *[Menudos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menudo_(band) "Menudo (band)") of Morumbi*, a team that included [Paulo Silas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Silas "Paulo Silas"), [Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müller_(footballer,_born_1966) "Müller (footballer, born 1966)") and Sidney, and the club once again won the Paulista Championship. The main striker was [Careca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Careca "Careca"), a centre-forward who also played for [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") in the [1986 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup "1986 FIFA World Cup"). The midfield featured [Falcão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Roberto_Falcão "Paulo Roberto Falcão"), brought in from Italian club [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma") and becoming a big part in winning the Campeonato Paulista in 1985*.* In [1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "1986 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), manager [Pepe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_(footballer,_born_1935) "Pepe (footballer, born 1935)") led the club to its second Brazilian Championship title, defeating [Guarani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guarani_Futebol_Clube "Guarani Futebol Clube") in a penalty shoot-out. In 1987, Dario Pereyra left the club, but in that year the *Menudos* team won its last title, another Paulista title. The so-called *Tricolor Decade* ended with the 1989 Paulista Championship title and a second-place finish in the Brazilian Championship, when São Paulo lost to [Vasco da Gama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CR_Vasco_da_Gama "CR Vasco da Gama") in the final match.[[22]](#cite_note-80s-22)

### 1990–1995: The Telê Era: Libertadores and Intercontinental Cups

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 1990–1995: The Telê Era: Libertadores and Intercontinental Cups")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Tel%C3%AA_Santana_da_Silva_01.jpg/250px-Tel%C3%AA_Santana_da_Silva_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Telê_Santana_da_Silva_01.jpg)

[Telê Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telê_Santana "Telê Santana"), won two Copa Libertadores and two Club World Cups with São Paulo.

In 1990, after a poor start to the campaign in the Paulista, [Telê Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telê_Santana "Telê Santana") was hired as the club's coach, and São Paulo went on to finish runners-up in the Brazilian Championship.[[23]](#cite_note-Tele-23) In 1991, Santana won his first title after winning the Paulista championship.

In 1991, São Paulo won the Brazilian championship after beating [Carlos Alberto Parreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Alberto_Parreira "Carlos Alberto Parreira")'s [Bragantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atlético_Bragantino "Clube Atlético Bragantino"), and the club began a period of consistent achievement both nationally and internationally. The following year they reached the [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") final, where they faced [Newell's Old Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newell's_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys") of Argentina. São Paulo lost the first leg 1–0, but reversed the scoreline in the second leg in Brazil, and then won the competition in the penalty shoot-out to take the title for the first time.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Ra%C3%AD_Souza_Vieira_de_Oliveira_01.jpg/250px-Ra%C3%AD_Souza_Vieira_de_Oliveira_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raí_Souza_Vieira_de_Oliveira_01.jpg)

[Raí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raí "Raí"), São Paulo's midfielder in the 1990s.

In the same year, in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo") the club won its first [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European/South_American_Cup "European/South American Cup"), beating [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff")'s [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") 2–1. After returning to Brazil, the club beat Palmeiras 2–1 to win its 18th state championship title.

In 1993, São Paulo retained the Copa Libertadores, beating [Universidad Católica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Deportivo_Universidad_Católica "Club Deportivo Universidad Católica") of [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile") in [the finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "1993 Copa Libertadores Finals") 5–3 on aggregate, including a 5–1 first leg win. After the competition, influential midfielder [Raí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raí "Raí") left the club. The Copa Libertadores win allowed the club to play the [Recopa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Recopa_Sudamericana "1993 Recopa Sudamericana") that year, beating [1992 Supercopa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Supercopa_Libertadores "1992 Supercopa Libertadores") winners and fellow Brazilian side Cruzeiro. The club also won the [1993 Supercopa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Supercopa_Libertadores "1993 Supercopa Libertadores"), beating Flamengo on penalties in the final. The Supercopa Libertadores title meant the club has completed an unprecedented CONMEBOL treble (Copa Libertadores, Recopa Sudamericana, Supercopa Libertadores).

São Paulo was able to defend its [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Intercontinental_Cup "1993 Intercontinental Cup") title again, beating [Fabio Capello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Capello "Fabio Capello")'s [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2. Müller scored the winning goal in the 86th minute of the match, from an assist by [Toninho Cerezo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toninho_Cerezo "Toninho Cerezo").[[25]](#cite_note-World_Title_93-25) This meant the club had completed a quadruple.

In 1994, the club reached the [Copa Libertadores finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "1994 Copa Libertadores Finals") for the third year in a row, and faced Argentina's [Vélez Sársfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_Vélez_Sársfield "Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield"). On this occasion they lost on penalties to the Argentine side at the Morumbi stadium. But by the end of this year, São Paulo won the [Copa CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_CONMEBOL "Copa CONMEBOL"), defeating Peñarol of Uruguay in [the finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Copa_CONMEBOL_finals "1994 Copa CONMEBOL finals") 6-4 on aggregate with a team known as "Expressinho", a team formed of youth and reserve players led by [Muricy Ramalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muricy_Ramalho "Muricy Ramalho").[[26]](#cite_note-26)

### 1996–2004: Post-Telê years

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 1996–2004: Post-Telê years")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Rogerio_ceni.jpg/250px-Rogerio_ceni.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rogerio_ceni.jpg)

[Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogério_Ceni "Rogério Ceni"), São Paulo's former goalkeeper, he is the [highest scoring goalkeeper of all time.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_goalscoring_goalkeepers "List of goalscoring goalkeepers")

At the beginning of 1996, owing to health issues, Telê Santana left São Paulo, ending the club's golden era. Between 1995 and 2004, the club had fourteen managers. Among the most notable titles during those ten years were the 2000 Paulista Championship and the club's first [Rio-São Paulo Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torneio_Rio-São_Paulo "Torneio Rio-São Paulo") title in 2001. [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogério_Ceni "Rogério Ceni"), [Júlio Baptista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Júlio_Baptista "Júlio Baptista"), [Luís Fabiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luís_Fabiano "Luís Fabiano") and [Kaká](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaká "Kaká") were the club's stars. Raí briefly returned to the club between 1998 and 2000, and with him, the club won the Paulista Championship twice, in 1998 and 2000, after beating Corinthians and Santos, respectively. In 2004 São Paulo were back in the Copa Libertadores and reached the semi-finals before being eliminated by underdogs [Once Caldas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once_Caldas "Once Caldas") from Colombia. At the end of that year, [Émerson Leão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Émerson_Leão "Émerson Leão") was hired as the club's coach.

In 2003, São Paulo made a deal with Spanish amateur side Santangelo Club Aficionado that resulted in the Spanish club changing its name to *[São Paulo Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo_Madrid "São Paulo Madrid")*.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

### 2005–2009: Three Brazilian Championships, Libertadores and FIFA Club World Cup

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2005–2009: Three Brazilian Championships, Libertadores and FIFA Club World Cup")]

In 2005, with Leão as the club's manager, São Paulo won the Paulista Championship. Leão, however, would soon leave the club with [Paulo Autuori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Autuori_de_Mello "Paulo Autuori de Mello"), former manager of the [Peru national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru_national_football_team "Peru national football team"), hired to replace him. São Paulo won the Libertadores Cup for the third time, beating another Brazilian side, [Atlético Paranaense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atlético_Paranaense "Clube Atlético Paranaense"), in the final. Atlético switched the first leg of the final to [Estádio Beira-Rio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_Beira-Rio "Estádio Beira-Rio"), [Porto Alegre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto_Alegre "Porto Alegre"), their own ground not having sufficient capacity for a final, and the match ended in a 1–1 draw. In the second leg, at the Morumbi, São Paulo won 4–0 to become the first Brazilian club to win three Copa Libertadores titles.

In December 2005, São Paulo competed in the [FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship "2005 FIFA Club World Championship") in Japan. After beating [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia")'s [Al-Ittihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ittihad_(Jeddah) "Al-Ittihad (Jeddah)") 3–2, they faced European champions [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in the final. A 1–0 victory over the English team gave São Paulo its third intercontinental title. The single goal was scored by [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)") in the first half of the match.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29) Other players in that year's squad included centre-back [Diego Lugano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Lugano "Diego Lugano"), full-back [Cicinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicinho "Cicinho"), forward [Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Márcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso"), and the record-breaking goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogério_Ceni "Rogério Ceni"), who was selected [Man of the Match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_match "Player of the match") at the [FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship "2005 FIFA Club World Championship") title match, as well as the tournament's [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_valuable_player "Most valuable player").[[30]](#cite_note-30)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg/330px-SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg)

Tribute received from the Paulista Football Federation and President Lula for winning their first FIFA Club World Cup.

After the success of the 2005 season, Paulo Autuori left the team to coach [Kashima Antlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashima_Antlers "Kashima Antlers") in the [J. League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._League_Division_1 "J. League Division 1"). [Muricy Ramalho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muricy_Ramalho "Muricy Ramalho") was signed up as the new coach, having led [Internacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Internacional "Sport Club Internacional") to the runners-up position in the 2005 Brazilian Championship. In his first tournament as a manager, Ramalho reached second place in the Paulista Championship, losing to Santos by one point. São Paulo reached the final of the [2006 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Copa_Libertadores "2006 Copa Libertadores"), but lost 4–3 on aggregate to Brazilian rivals [Internacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Internacional "Sport Club Internacional"). However, they went on to win their fourth [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2006 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") trophy, becoming the first team to become national champions in the new [league system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_system "League system") format.

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Bayern_vs_Sao_Paulo_at_Hong_Kong.jpg/250px-Bayern_vs_Sao_Paulo_at_Hong_Kong.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bayern_vs_Sao_Paulo_at_Hong_Kong.jpg)

São Paulo against [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayern_Munich "Bayern Munich") in 2007.

After being eliminated from the [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Copa_Libertadores "2007 Copa Libertadores") round of 16 to [Grêmio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grêmio_Foot-Ball_Porto_Alegrense "Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense") in 2007, São Paulo won the Brazilian title for the second year in a row, fifteen points ahead of second-placed [Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_FC "Santos FC"). They won the title for the third season running in 2008 season, overturning an 11-point deficit behind Grêmio in the second half, to win its sixth league title. Manager Muricy Ramalho was the first manager to win three league titles in a row with the same team.

Despite this feat, Muricy was sacked the following year after São Paulo was eliminated in the [2009 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Copa_Libertadores "2009 Copa Libertadores") quarter-finals to Cruzeiro, its fourth consecutive elimination to a Brazilian side. [Ricardo Gomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Gomes "Ricardo Gomes") took over as manager. The club was very close to winning the league for the fourth time in a row, however, after struggling in the final 4 games, they ended up finishing in third.

### 2010–2020: Copa Sudamericana and a tough period

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2010–2020: Copa Sudamericana and a tough period")]

In 2010 São Paulo lost once again to [Internacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Internacional "Sport Club Internacional") in the [2010 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Copa_Libertadores "2010 Copa Libertadores"), this time in the semifinals, ending [Ricardo Gomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Gomes "Ricardo Gomes")' spell as manager. The club finished ninth in the league, not qualifying for the international competition for the first time since 2003.

In 2011, the club signed [Rivaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivaldo "Rivaldo") and brought back [Luís Fabiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luís_Fabiano "Luís Fabiano") for a club-record €7.6 million from [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogério_Ceni "Rogério Ceni"), meanwhile, scored his 100th career goal, against Corinthians in the Campeonato Paulista. Despite these events, it was another very disappointing season, finishing sixth in the league and failing to qualify for the Libertadores once again.

In research conducted by Brazilian sports website GloboEsporte.com, São Paulo, during the eight years between 2003 and 2011, were just the second Brazilian club to earn more money than losses in the transfer market – *Tricolor paulista* received [R$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real")287 million, behind only Internacional, which earned R$289 million.[[31]](#cite_note-31)

In 2012, São Paulo won the [Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Sudamericana "Copa Sudamericana") (its only title in the 2010 decade) and qualified for next season's Libertadores, finishing fourth in the league under [Ney Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ney_Franco "Ney Franco"). However, after that season, the club hit a second massive dry spell and struggled to regain its dominance in the Brazilian and South American stage.

For the 2013 season, after seven years wearing kits produced by [Reebok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reebok "Reebok"), São Paulo signed with Brazilian brand [Penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_(Brazilian_sports_manufacturer) "Penalty (Brazilian sports manufacturer)"). The contract was valid until 2015 and the club earned R$35 million per year.[[32]](#cite_note-32) This contract was the second-most lucrative kit deal in Brazil, just exceeded by Flamengo and [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas")' deal of R$38 million.[[33]](#cite_note-33) In May 2015 São Paulo presented its new kits, made by [Under Armour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Armour "Under Armour"). In 2018 the team became sponsored by Adidas.[[34]](#cite_note-34)

In [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2014 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2018 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") and [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2020 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") the club was one of the contenders for the national league title, but did not win it; São Paulo finished runners-up in 2014, fifth in 2018, and fourth in 2020, the last two being marked by massives drops of form in the second half. In contrast to this, they struggled hard in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2013 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") and [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2017 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), fighting (and eventually saving themselves) against relegation to the [second tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_B "Campeonato Brasileiro Série B").

Continentally, in 2016 the club reached the semi-finals of the [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Copa_Libertadores "2016 Copa Libertadores"), losing to [Atlético Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlético_Nacional "Atlético Nacional").

During the 2010s, São Paulo did not win a single [Campeonato Paulista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeonato_Paulista "Campeonato Paulista") title, the first time since the 1960s.

### 2021–present: Champions of Everything

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2021–present: Champions of Everything")]

In 2021, São Paulo finally ended its second biggest dry spell in its history (8 years); under new manager [Hernán Crespo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hernán_Crespo "Hernán Crespo"), the club defeated [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedade_Esportiva_Palmeiras "Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras") at the [Campeonato Paulista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Campeonato_Paulista "2021 Campeonato Paulista") finals, winning the competition for the first time since 2005. However, after a continuing sequence of poor results, which included quarter-final exits in the [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores "2021 Copa Libertadores") and in the [Copa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_do_Brasil "2021 Copa do Brasil") to Palmeiras and [Fortaleza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortaleza_Esporte_Clube "Fortaleza Esporte Clube"), respectively, Crespo was sacked in October, with the club being involved in another relegation battle at the [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2021 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), eventually finishing 13th, after Crespo was replaced by club legend [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogério_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") in his second managerial spell.

In 2022, under Ceni, the club reached once again the [Campeonato Paulista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Campeonato_Paulista "2022 Campeonato Paulista") finals, reaching their third state finals in four years; a progress, since São Paulo didn't reach the state finals between 2007 (when the knock-out second phase was re-established) and 2018. São Paulo ended the competition as runners-up to Palmeiras; despite winning the first leg 3–1 at the Morumbi, they suffered a heavy 4–0 comeback defeat at Allianz Parque. Also in 2022, the club reached the semifinals of the [2022 Copa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Copa_do_Brasil "2022 Copa do Brasil"), being eliminated by eventual winners [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo "Clube de Regatas do Flamengo"),[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] and suffered another final defeat, this time in the [Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Copa_Sudamericana "2022 Copa Sudamericana"), losing to Ecuadorian side [Independiente del Valle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.S.D._Independiente_del_Valle "C.S.D. Independiente del Valle") in [Córdoba, Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Córdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina").[[35]](#cite_note-35) In the [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2022 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A"), however, São Paulo finished in 9th place, one position outside Copa Libertadores qualification.

In 2023, just like six years before, Rogério Ceni was sacked and replaced by [Dorival Júnior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorival_Júnior "Dorival Júnior") after getting eliminated in the quarter-final of the [Campeonato Paulista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Campeonato_Paulista "2023 Campeonato Paulista") to underdogs and eventual runners-up [Água Santa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esporte_Clube_Água_Santa "Esporte Clube Água Santa"). Under the guidance of Dorival, São Paulo won its first [Copa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Copa_do_Brasil "2023 Copa do Brasil") title in a memorable run, defeating along the way [Ituano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ituano_Futebol_Clube "Ituano Futebol Clube"), [Sport Recife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Recife "Sport Recife") and, most notably, city rivals Palmeiras and Corinthians and defending champions Flamengo in the finals, winning the first leg 1–0 in the [Maracanã](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maracanã_Stadium "Maracanã Stadium") and drawing 1–1 at the second leg in the Morumbi.[[36]](#cite_note-36) The club finished 11th in the [Campeonato Brasileiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Campeonato_Brasileiro_Série_A "2023 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") and reached the quarter-finals of the [Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Copa_Sudamericana "2023 Copa Sudamericana"), being eliminated by eventual champions [L.D.U. Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.D.U._Quito "L.D.U. Quito").

After a successful year, Dorival Júnior left São Paulo in January 2024 to manage the [Brazil national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"); it was the third time the club lost their manager to a national team in more than eight years (the others being [Juan Carlos Osorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Carlos_Osorio "Juan Carlos Osorio") to [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team "Mexico national football team") in 2015 and in the following year, [Edgardo Bauza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgardo_Bauza "Edgardo Bauza") to [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team")).[[37]](#cite_note-37) [Juventude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esporte_Clube_Juventude "Esporte Clube Juventude") manager [Thiago Carpini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Carpini "Thiago Carpini") was appointed as Dorival's replacement,[[38]](#cite_note-38) guiding the club to the [2024 Supercopa Rei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Supercopa_Rei "2024 Supercopa Rei") defeating Palmeiras on penalties at the [Mineirão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineirão "Mineirão") in [Belo Horizonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belo_Horizonte "Belo Horizonte").[[39]](#cite_note-39) With the Supercopa Rei title, São Paulo became the only team in Brazil to win all the competitions that are held and still exist in the [Brazilian football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Brazil "Football in Brazil") calendar, earning the nickname "Champions of Everything".[[40]](#cite_note-40)

At the beginning of 2026, president [Julio Casares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Casares "Julio Casares") was impeached and Harry Massis Júnior assumed in his place.[[41]](#cite_note-41) The club had a revenue of R$ 1,07 billion [reais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real") in 2025; in the same year the debt was lowered to R$ 858,2 million reais.[[42]](#cite_note-42) In May 2026 Dorival Júnior returned as manager, after the dismissal of [Roger Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Machado_(footballer) "Roger Machado (footballer)").[[43]](#cite_note-43) In September 2026, Julio Casares was expelled from São Paulo's membership rolls; the ex-president will have to pay compensation to the club.[[44]](#cite_note-44)

 [![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/AA_das_Palmeiras.svg/120px-AA_das_Palmeiras.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AA_das_Palmeiras.svg)

Associação Atlética das Palmeiras

When the [Club Athletico Paulistano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Athletico_Paulistano "Club Athletico Paulistano") and the [Associação Atlética das Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associação_Atlética_das_Palmeiras "Associação Atlética das Palmeiras") merged, their colours (red and white for CA Paulistano and black and white for AA das Palmeiras) were inherited by São Paulo. The colours match those of [São Paulo's state flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_São_Paulo_(state) "Flag of São Paulo (state)"),[[45]](#cite_note-45) and also represents the three main races that lived in Brazil during that period: the [Native Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Brazil "Indigenous peoples in Brazil") (represented by the red), the [White Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Brazilians "White Brazilians") (represented by the white) and the [Afro-Brazilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afro-Brazilians "Afro-Brazilians") (represented by the black).[[46]](#cite_note-46)

The club's home kit is a white shirt, with two horizontal stripes at chest level, the upper one red and the lower one black, and the badge in the centre of the chest; the shorts and socks are white. The away kit consists of a shirt with red, white and black vertical stripes, black shorts and black socks.

The badge, representing a [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart "Heart") with five points, consists of a shield with a black rectangle in the upper section bearing the initials SPFC in white; below the rectangle there's a red, white and black triangle. It was designed by the [german](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germans "Germans") graphic designer Walter Ostrich and one of the founders, Firmiano de Morais Pinto Filho.[[47]](#cite_note-47) The badge also has five stars, two gold and three red ones: the gold ones denote [Adhemar Ferreira da Silva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhemar_Ferreira_da_Silva "Adhemar Ferreira da Silva")'s World and Olympic records at the [1952 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics "1952 Summer Olympics") in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") and at the [1955 Pan American Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Pan_American_Games "1955 Pan American Games") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"); the red ones represent each of the two [Intercontinental Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960–2004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") and the [FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup "FIFA Club World Cup") won by the club.[[48]](#cite_note-48)

Although São Paulo's kit has been supplied by several different manufacturers, the club's traditional home and away kit suffered very few changes and variations throughout the years, making it one the most recognizable kits in Brazil.

The first sports equipment supplier in São Paulo's history was the brazilian company [Athleta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athleta_(association_football_brand) "Athleta (association football brand)") in 1960.[[49]](#cite_note-49) From 1986 to 1990, 1996 to 1999 and 2018 to 2023 the club was sponsored by the german company [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas").[[50]](#cite_note-50)[[51]](#cite_note-51) São Paulo was sponsored by american company [Reebok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reebok "Reebok") from 2006 to 2012, when signed a contract with brazilian [Penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_(brand) "Penalty (brand)") until 2015.[[52]](#cite_note-52)[[53]](#cite_note-53) American company [Under Armour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Armour "Under Armour") sponsored the club from 2015 to the end of 2017.[[54]](#cite_note-54) From 2024 until 2032, the club has a contract with american sports equipment supplier [New Balance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Balance "New Balance").[[55]](#cite_note-55)

## Stadium

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Estádio do Morumbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estádio_do_Morumbi "Estádio do Morumbi")

[![Aerial view of the Morumbi Stadium.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Est%C3%A1dio_do_Morumbi.jpg/330px-Est%C3%A1dio_do_Morumbi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estádio_do_Morumbi.jpg)

Aerial view of the Morumbi Stadium.

São Paulo's iconic 72,039 seater stadium is officially named *Estádio Cícero Pompeu de Toledo* (Cicero Pompeu de Toledo Stadium) and commonly known by the nickname *Estádio do Morumbi* (Morumbi Stadium). It was designed by architect [Vilanova Artigas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilanova_Artigas "Vilanova Artigas") and it's considered a monument in [Brazilian modernism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism_in_Brazil "Modernism in Brazil"). Due to its significant cultural and architectural importance, [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo")'s administration chose to include the stadium in its cultural preservation list, effectively eliminating any chance of modification and modernization in the stadium.

MorumBIS has been on the list since 2018, but after the signature of a multi-million refurbishment deal with [WTorre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTorre?action=edit&redlink=1 "WTorre (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/WTorre "pt:WTorre")], São Paulo's prefecture agreed to withdraw the stadium's name for the list, paving the way for a R$800 million modernization to be complete by 2030.

In late 2023, [Mondelez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mondelez_International "Mondelez International") bought the [Naming rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naming_rights "Naming rights") to the stadium for a record R$25 million a year, on a 5-year contract, temporarily changing the stadium's name to "MorumBIS". Also in 2023, [Live Nation Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation_Entertainment "Live Nation Entertainment") signed a R$ 60 million 5-year deal with the club for concerts and events in the Stadium, the deal being the most expensive of its kind.

The first game played at the stadium was on 2 October 1960, when São Paulo won 1–0 in a friendly match against [Sporting Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_CP "Sporting CP") from Portugal. It was inaugurated in with a maximum sitting capacity of 120,000 people, but now its maximum capacity is 72,039 seats.[[56]](#cite_note-Morumbi-56)

The club also owns two training grounds, one named *Centro de Treinamento Frederico Antônio Germano Menzen* (Frederico Antônio Germano Menzen Training Center), nicknamed *Centro de Treinamento (CT) da Barra Funda* (Barra Funda's Training Center), which is used mostly by the professional team.[[57]](#cite_note-ctbarrafunda-57) The other is the *Centro de Formação de Atletas Presidente Laudo Natel* (President Laudo Natel Athletes Formation Center), nicknamed *Centro de Treinamento (CT) de Cotia* (Cotia's Training Center), which is used by the youth teams.[[58]](#cite_note-Cotia-58)

## Club rivalries

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Club rivalries")]

### *São Paulo vs. Corinthians*

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: São Paulo vs. Corinthians")]

Main article: [Clássico Majestoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clássico_Majestoso "Clássico Majestoso")

The game between these clubs is also known as "Majestoso", a name coined by Thomas Mazzoni. The first "Majestoso" occurred on 25 May 1930. The fixture has seen 110 wins for São Paulo, 131 wins for Corinthians and 114 draws.[[66]](#cite_note-66)

### *São Paulo vs. Palmeiras*

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: São Paulo vs. Palmeiras")]

Main article: [Choque-Rei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choque-Rei "Choque-Rei")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Palmeiras_x_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_-_Allianz_Parque.jpg/250px-Palmeiras_x_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_-_Allianz_Parque.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palmeiras_x_São_Paulo_-_Allianz_Parque.jpg)

First Choque-Rei in Allianz Parque in March 2015

This fixture is nicknamed the "Choque Rei", and has seen 114 wins by São Paulo, 113 wins by Palmeiras and 110 draws.[[67]](#cite_note-67)

### *São Paulo vs. Santos*

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: São Paulo vs. Santos")]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Lance_de_Santos_3_x_2_S%C3%A3o_Paulo%2C_partida_v%C3%A1lida_pelo_Brasileir%C3%A3o_2017%2C_disputada_na_Vila_Belmiro_%2835660102752%29.jpg/250px-Lance_de_Santos_3_x_2_S%C3%A3o_Paulo%2C_partida_v%C3%A1lida_pelo_Brasileir%C3%A3o_2017%2C_disputada_na_Vila_Belmiro_%2835660102752%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lance_de_Santos_3_x_2_São_Paulo,_partida_válida_pelo_Brasileirão_2017,_disputada_na_Vila_Belmiro_(35660102752).jpg)

Main article: [San-São](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San-São "San-São")

Also known as "San-São", this fixture was first played in 1936. Since then, São Paulo have won it 137 times, Santos 106, and there have been 75 draws.[[68]](#cite_note-68)

## Honours

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Honours")]

Main article: [List of São Paulo FC records and statistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_São_Paulo_FC_records_and_statistics "List of São Paulo FC records and statistics")

São Paulo FC is one of the most successful clubs in Brazil, having won a total of 32 domestic honours, in addition to their 12 international successes. It is the Brazilian club with the most international titles. By winning the [2024 Supercopa do Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Supercopa_do_Brasil "2024 Supercopa do Brasil"), São Paulo became the first Brazilian club to win all available trophies.[[3]](#cite_note-PlacarFeb24-3)

conteudo:
No mbito mundial, apenas dez times conquistaram dez ou mais títulos internacionais, o São Paulo foi o oitavo time que conquistou dez títulos internacionais oficiais, além disso, é o sétimo time a conquistar mais de dez títulos. No continente sul-americano, ele foi o terceiro time a realizar tal feito.

, Copa Libertadores da América (três títulos), Copa Intercontinental (dois títulos) e Copa do Mundo de Clubes da FIFA (um título).

No que diz respeito ao somatório de títulos oficiais de abrangência nacional e internacional de clubes brasileiros de futebol, o São Paulo figura como o terceiro maior campeão do Brasil, com 20 conquistas, atrás do Flamengo (22) e do Palmeiras (24). [...] | Competição | Títulos | Temporadas |
| Copa do Mundo de Clubes da FIFA | 1 | 2005 |
| Copa Intercontinental | 2 | 1992 e 1993 |

| Copa Libertadores da América | 3 | 1992, 1993 e 2005 |
| Copa Sul-Americana | 1 | 2012 |
| Recopa Sul-Americana | 2 | 1993 e 1994 |
| Supercopa Libertadores | 1 | 1993 |

| Estaduais |
| Competição | Títulos | Temporadas | [...] O São Paulo FC chegou a conquistar sete títulos com sua equipe principal em 1993, quando o Tricolor do Morumbi foi campeão da Copa Libertadores, da Supercopa Sul-Americana, da Recopa Sul-Americana, do Copa Europeia/Sul-Americana de 1993 e dos torneios Ciudad de Santiago, Santiago de Compostela e Troféu Jalisco. Já conquistou duas tríplices coroas, em 1992 e 2005, com dois títulos continentais e um estadual, e a quádrupla coroa internacional uma vez, em 1993, com três títulos continentais e um mundial.
